text: The scan's grammar matches every surface it is applied to. refuse_external runs on THREE surfaces -- theme.css, theme.js and layout.html (artifact/theme.rs:201-206) -- and strip_comments implements CSS's comment and string grammar, which JS and HTML do not share. MEASURED 2026-09-09 by vc at the artifact, both arms, and the mismatch runs in BOTH directions where the row was minted believing it ran in one. OVER-refusal, loud: a theme.js attribution in a // comment and an HTML attribution in <!-- --> are both refused, the harm the comment exemption exists to prevent. UNDER-refusal, silent: a live href in layout.html between a stray /* and a later */ is stripped before the scan and SHIPS -- issue 0018, the class of 0014, 0015 and 0017 on the surface none of them looked at. RULED BY VC IN TWO PARTS, SIZED TO WHICH HALF IS SILENT. NOW: the comment exemption becomes CSS-only, and a non-CSS surface is scanned with no comment stripping at all. That closes the silent half outright -- nothing can be hidden behind markers the language does not have -- and costs a flag on one call. LATER, and only once a real theme.js or layout.html exists in the estate: a comment and string grammar per surface, which is cc's shape and the right one at that point. What remains after the first part is over-refusal on every comment in JS and HTML, and it fails LOUDLY against a population of zero -- nine theme.css files estate-wide, no theme.js, no layout.html -- which is what makes it deferrable where the bypass was not. NOT dischargeable by writing down that the CSS scanner is adequate, because it is not.

state.evidence: FIXED AT cc 538e7fe AND VERIFIED BY vc AT THE ARTIFACT, four arms, exit codes read directly rather than through a pipe. The grammar is now chosen per call site: Grammar::Css strips comments as before, Grammar::Verbatim scans every byte, and artifact/theme.rs passes Css for theme.css, Verbatim for theme.js and Verbatim for layout.html. No per-surface JS or HTML comment parsers were built, per hv -- the population is nine theme.css, zero theme.js, zero layout.html. FOUR FIXTURES, BUILT AND RUN AGAINST THE REAL BINARY, each fixture's content proved present before its result was read: (A) a clean layout.html BUILDS, exit 0, artifact written -- the control, without which a refusal for an unrelated reason is indistinguishable from the fix; (B) issue 0018's bypass fixture verbatim, the live href between a stray /* on line 1 and a */ on line 3, REFUSES at exit 2 with no artifact, naming layout.html, the http:// scheme, the offending line and LINE 2 -- and line 2 can only be reported if the line-1 marker stripped nothing, so the message itself carries the proof; (C) a /* */ attribution in theme.js REFUSES at exit 2, which is the COST and is loud, where it built yesterday; (D) the same attribution in theme.css BUILDS at exit 0, so the CSS exemption is preserved and the narrowing did not over-correct. THE 2x2 IS THE POINT: the silent bypass closed, the loud cost accepted, the CSS half unchanged, and a clean control proving the harness path works at all. cc also pinned the defect in their suite -- the bypass under Grammar::Css is asserted to STILL BUILD -- so a later per-surface parser must come and delete that assertion deliberately rather than meet it as a failure.
